sections.title: Collocations with MAKE
sections.content:
MAKE is used for creating, producing, or causing something:
• make a decision — We need to make a decision by tomorrow.
• make an effort — You should make more effort in your studies.
• make progress — The students are making great progress this term.
• make a mistake — Everyone makes mistakes; it's how you learn.
• make an impression — She made a lasting impression at the interview.
• make a complaint — I'd like to make a formal complaint about the service.
• make arrangements — We've made arrangements for the conference next week.

sections.title: Collocations with DO
sections.content:
DO is used for tasks, activities, and work:
• do research — Scientists did extensive research on the vaccine.
• do damage — The storm did considerable damage to the coastline.
• do business — Our company does business in over 30 countries.
• do someone a favour — Could you do me a favour and check my essay?
• do your best — Just do your best and don't worry about the result.
• do harm — Spreading rumours can do real harm to people.
• do justice — This photo doesn't do justice to the beautiful view.

exercises.question: Which is correct: ___ a decision?
exercises.explanation: We say make a decision, not 'do a decision'.

exercises.question: Which is correct: ___ a mistake?
exercises.explanation: We say make a mistake, not 'do a mistake'.

exercises.question: Which is correct: ___ your best?
exercises.explanation: We say do your best, not 'make your best'.

exercises.question: Which is correct: ___ business with someone?
Which is correct: ___ damage to something?
Which is correct: ___ an impression?
exercises.hint: Creating a lasting image in someone's mind.
exercises.explanation: We say make an impression, not 'do an impression' (which means imitating someone).
